title: McDonald's Is Secretly a Landlord
summary: 95% of McDonald's restaurants are run by franchisees who pay it rent and royalties. Here's why the land under the restaurants matters more than the burgers.

hooks.hook: In McDonald's early years, a finance man brought Ray Kroc an idea: own the land, rent it to the franchisees.
McDonald's is a landlord that sells burgers.
95% of McDonald's restaurants aren't run by McDonald's.

sources: McDonald's 2025 Form 10-K (Item 1): "Of the 45,356 McDonald's restaurants at year-end 2025, approximately 95% were franchised"; conventional franchisees pay "rent and royalties based upon a percent of sales, with specified minimum rent payments"; the Company "generally owns or secures a long-term lease on the land and building"; operating margin 46.1%; systemwide sales $139.4 billion: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/63908/000006390826000035/mcd-20251231.htm

McDonald's fourth quarter and full year 2025 results (Feb 11, 2026), income statement: revenues from franchised restaurants $16,548M; company-owned and operated sales $9,690M; franchised occupancy expenses $2,618M; company-operated restaurant expenses $8,268M; operating income $12,393M; net income $8,563M: https://mcdonalds.mediaroom.com/2026-02-11-McDONALDS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS
Our calculations: franchised margin $16,548M - $2,618M = $13,930M; company-operated margin $9,690M - $8,268M = $1,422M (about 9.8x).
Harry J. Sonneborn proposed that Kroc own the land under McDonald's restaurants and lease it to franchisees: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_J._Sonneborn
Kroc bought the McDonald brothers' stake in 1961 for $2.7 million; at end-2025 the company owned about 56% of the land and 80% of the restaurant buildings: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald%27s

scenes.narration: In McDonald's early years, a finance man named Harry Sonneborn brought Ray Kroc an idea. Don't just sell franchises. Own the land under them, and rent it to the franchisees.
It may have been the most important money decision McDonald's ever made.
Today, about {95 percent|ninety-five percent} of McDonald's {45,356|forty-five thousand three hundred fifty-six} restaurants are run by franchisees, not by McDonald's.
And most of the money McDonald's makes from them doesn't come from selling burgers. It comes from being their landlord.
Part one. The rent check.
Here's the deal a franchisee signs. They pay rent and a royalty, both based on a percent of their sales, with a minimum rent even in a bad month.
Think about what that means. When a restaurant has a great year, the rent grows with its sales. When it has a bad year, McDonald's still collects the minimum.
McDonald's usually owns the land and the building, or holds a long lease on them. The franchisee pays to cook in it.

lines.text: You pay to cook in it

scenes.narration: At the end of {2025,|twenty twenty-five,} McDonald's owned about {56 percent|fifty-six percent} of the land under its restaurants, and {80 percent|eighty percent} of the buildings.
If you like seeing the receipts behind everyday prices, subscribe. New ones every Tuesday and Friday.
Part two. Follow the money.

In {2025,|twenty twenty-five,} franchisees paid McDonald's {$16.5 billion.|sixteen point five billion dollars.} The restaurants McDonald's runs itself sold {$9.7 billion|nine point seven billion} of food.
Now take away the costs. The franchise side left {$13.9 billion.|thirteen point nine billion.} McDonald's own restaurants left {$1.4 billion.|one point four billion.}
Rent doesn't need a grill, a fryer, or a night shift.
That's almost ten times more, from restaurants it doesn't even run.
That's why, out of every dollar McDonald's takes in, about {46 cents|forty-six cents} is operating profit.
Part three. The brothers' price.
In {1961,|nineteen sixty-one,} Ray Kroc bought out the McDonald brothers for {$2.7 million.|two point seven million dollars.}
Last year, McDonald's restaurants around the world sold {$139.4 billion|one hundred thirty-nine point four billion dollars} of food.
Most of it rang up in restaurants McDonald's doesn't run, on land it often owns.
So the next time your local McDonald's raises its prices, remember who gets a cut of every sale: the landlord.
McDonald's sells burgers. But the business is the ground under them. Next time: why the printer is the bait.
